question: According to the census of India 2011, which state has the lowest population growth rate?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Nagaland.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• As per Census 2011, Nagaland recorded the lowest decadal population growth rate among all Indian states — in fact a negative growth rate of about -0.47% (2001-2011). (जनसंख्या वृद्धि दर — नागालैंड)

 

• This was the first time in India's census history that any state recorded a negative decadal growth rate; the fall is widely attributed to correction of earlier over-reported figures and improved enumeration.

 

• India's overall decadal population growth rate for 2001-2011 was 17.64%, making Nagaland's figure a striking outlier among the states.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Meghalaya recorded one of the highest decadal growth rates (about 27.82%) among the north-eastern states in the same census.

 

• Kerala has traditionally recorded comparatively low growth rates due to high literacy and lower fertility, though it did not record negative growth.

 

NOTE

 

• Jharkhand (Option 1): Recorded a decadal growth rate of about 22.34%, well above the national trend.

 

• Punjab (Option 2): Recorded a moderate decadal growth rate of about 13.89%, not the lowest.

 

• Uttar Pradesh (Option 3): Recorded a decadal growth rate of about 20.09%, among the higher-growth large states.

question: In 2023, Praveen Chithravel won the men’s triple jump event at the ‘Prueba de Confrontacion’ athletics meet held in ___________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Cuba.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Indian triple jumper Praveen Chithravel won the men's triple jump event and set a new national record (17.37 m) at the 'Prueba de Confrontacion' athletics meet held in Havana, Cuba, in May 2023. (त्रिकूद स्पर्धा — प्रवीण चित्रवेल, क्यूबा)

 

• With this performance he broke the long-standing national record and qualified for the 2023 World Athletics Championships held in Budapest, Hungary.

 

• He surpassed the earlier national triple jump record held by Arpinder Singh.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Praveen Chithravel, from Tamil Nadu, also won a bronze medal in the men's triple jump at the 2022 Commonwealth Games in Birmingham.

 

• At that same Commonwealth Games, fellow Indians Eldhose Paul (gold) and Abdulla Aboobacker (silver) completed a historic triple-jump podium sweep for India.

 

NOTE

 

• Canada, Brazil, Portugal (Options 1, 3, 4): None of these is the host of the 'Prueba de Confrontacion' meet, which is an annual athletics meet held in Havana, Cuba.

question: Which is the waterbody that separates Andaman Islands and Nicobar Islands?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Ten Degree Channel.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Ten Degree Channel, roughly 150 km wide and running along the 10°N latitude, separates the Andaman Islands (to the north) from the Nicobar Islands (to the south). (दस डिग्री चैनल — अंडमान और निकोबार)

 

• It connects the Bay of Bengal with the Andaman Sea and is an important international shipping route.

 

• Further south, the Great Channel separates the Nicobar Islands (India) from Sumatra, Indonesia.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Within the Andaman Islands, the Duncan Passage separates South Andaman from Little Andaman.

 

• The Andaman and Nicobar Islands together form a Union Territory of India in the Bay of Bengal.

 

NOTE

 

• Eight Degree Channel (Option 1): Separates Minicoy Island from the Maldives.

 

• Nine Degree Channel (Option 2): Separates the Lakshadweep islands from Minicoy Island.

 

• Eleven Degree Channel (Option 4): Separates the Amindivi group from the Cannanore/Laccadive group within Lakshadweep, not Andaman from Nicobar.

question: According to the Census 2011 of India, which metropolitan has the second highest population?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Delhi.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• As per Census 2011, the Mumbai Urban Agglomeration had the highest population in India (about 1.84 crore), followed by the Delhi Urban Agglomeration with the second highest population (about 1.63 crore). (जनसंख्या के अनुसार महानगर — दिल्ली)

 

• The Kolkata Urban Agglomeration ranked third (about 1.41 crore), and Chennai ranked fourth (about 87 lakh).

 

• Rankings by urban agglomeration population are a standard Census 2011 fact frequently asked in general awareness sections.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Bengaluru Urban Agglomeration ranked fifth by population as per Census 2011.

 

• Delhi is administered as the National Capital Territory (NCT) of Delhi.

 

NOTE

 

• Kolkata (Option 1): Ranked third by population, not second.

 

• Mumbai (Option 2): Ranked first (highest), not second.

 

• Chennai (Option 3): Ranked fourth by population.

question: Which Article provides that all minorities have the right to establish and administer educational institutions of their choice?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Article 30.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Article 30 of the Indian Constitution grants all minorities, whether based on religion or language, the right to establish and administer educational institutions of their choice. (अनुच्छेद 30 — अल्पसंख्यक शिक्षा अधिकार)

 

• It falls under Part III (Fundamental Rights), specifically among the Cultural and Educational Rights (Articles 29-30).

 

• It also bars the State from discriminating against minority-run institutions while granting aid.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Article 29 protects the right of any section of citizens to conserve its distinct language, script or culture.

 

• Article 350A directs States to provide facilities for instruction in the mother tongue at the primary stage.

 

NOTE

 

• Article 26 (Option 1): Grants every religious denomination the freedom to manage its own religious affairs, not to run educational institutions specifically.

 

• Article 24 (Option 2): Prohibits employment of children below 14 years in factories, mines or other hazardous occupations.

 

• Article 32 (Option 3): Provides the right to constitutional remedies, allowing citizens to approach the Supreme Court to enforce fundamental rights.

question: What is the IUPAC name of the compound CH3NH2?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Methanamine.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• CH3NH2 (commonly called methylamine) is the simplest primary aliphatic amine, formed by replacing one hydrogen atom of methane with an -NH2 group; its IUPAC name is Methanamine. (मेथेनामिन — CH3NH2 का IUPAC नाम)

 

• By IUPAC convention, primary amines are named by adding the suffix '-amine' to the name of the parent alkane (dropping the final 'e' where required), so methane + amine gives methanamine.

 

• Methylamine is a colourless, flammable gas with a strong ammonia-like odour, widely used as an intermediate in the chemical and pharmaceutical industries.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Similarly, C2H5NH2 (ethylamine) has the IUPAC name Ethanamine, and C3H7NH2 (n-propylamine) has the IUPAC name Propan-1-amine.

 

• Amines are classified as primary, secondary or tertiary depending on the number of carbon groups attached to the nitrogen atom.

 

NOTE

 

• Propan-1-amine (Option 1): This is the IUPAC name of n-propylamine (C3H7NH2), a three-carbon amine, not CH3NH2.

 

• 2-Methyl propan-1-amine (Option 3): This is the IUPAC name of isobutylamine ((CH3)2CHCH2NH2), a four-carbon branched amine.

 

• Ethanamine (Option 4): This is the IUPAC name of ethylamine (C2H5NH2), a two-carbon amine, not CH3NH2.

question: As of March, 2024, who is the minister of the Ministry of Cooperation, Government of India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Amit Shah.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Ministry of Cooperation was created as a separate Union ministry in July 2021, and Amit Shah was appointed its first Union Minister, in addition to holding the Ministry of Home Affairs. (सहकारिता मंत्रालय — अमित शाह)

 

• As of March 2024, Amit Shah continued to hold charge of both the Home Affairs and Cooperation portfolios.

 

• The ministry works under the vision of 'Sahkar se Samriddhi' ('Prosperity through Cooperation') to strengthen the cooperative movement in India.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Ministry of Cooperation was carved out of the erstwhile Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare, which used to handle cooperative-sector matters.

 

• Key initiatives under this ministry include computerisation of Primary Agricultural Credit Societies (PACS) and setting up new multipurpose cooperative societies.

 

NOTE

 

• Smriti Zubin Irani (Option 1): Held the Ministry of Women and Child Development and Ministry of Minority Affairs during this period.

 

• Dharmendra Pradhan (Option 3): Held the Ministry of Education and Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship.

 

• Nitin Gadkari (Option 4): Held the Ministry of Road Transport and Highways.

question: Which amongst the following statements is correct about Mughal emperor Akbar?
option_2: He founded a new religion called ‘Din-e Ilahi’.
option_3: He was highly educated and knew many languages.
option_4: He fought and won the third battle of Panipat against the Hindu King Hemu.
solution_text:
The correct answer is He founded a new religion called 'Din-e Ilahi'.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Mughal emperor Akbar founded a syncretic religious order called Din-e Ilahi ('Religion of God') in 1582 CE, drawing elements from Islam, Hinduism, Zoroastrianism, Christianity and Jainism. (दीन-ए-इलाही — अकबर)

 

• Akbar became emperor in 1556 CE, after the death of his father Humayun, at the age of about 13 — not 1602.

 

• Although a great patron of learning, Akbar himself is widely recorded by historians as being largely illiterate; he acquired knowledge by having texts read aloud to him, so he was not conventionally 'highly educated and knowing many languages' in the sense of reading/writing them.

 

• Akbar fought and won the Second Battle of Panipat (1556) against Hemu (Hemchandra Vikramaditya), not the third.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Akbar abolished the jizya tax on non-Muslims in 1564 and established the Ibadat Khana (House of Worship) at Fatehpur Sikri for interfaith discourse.

 

• The Third Battle of Panipat (1761) was fought between the Marathas and Ahmad Shah Abdali, long after Akbar's reign.

 

NOTE

 

• Option 1: Incorrect — Akbar became emperor in 1556, not 1602.

 

• Option 3: Incorrect — Akbar is historically recorded as being unable to read or write, despite being a great patron of art and literature.

 

• Option 4: Incorrect — Akbar's victory over Hemu was in the Second Battle of Panipat (1556), not the third.

question: Which of the following is an example of system software?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Windows operating system.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• System software manages and controls a computer's hardware so that application software can run on it; the operating system, such as Windows, is the primary example of system software. (सिस्टम सॉफ्टवेयर — विंडोज़ ऑपरेटिंग सिस्टम)

 

• System software works in the background, providing a platform for application programs, and includes the OS, device drivers, and utility programs.

 

• Application software (like word processors, browsers, and image editors) is designed to help the end user perform specific tasks and runs on top of system software.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other examples of system software include device drivers, firmware, compilers/linkers, and other operating systems like Linux and macOS.

 

• System software is typically installed first and is essential for the computer to function at all.

 

NOTE

 

• Adobe Photoshop (Option 2): An application software used for image editing.

 

• Microsoft Word (Option 3): An application software used for word processing.

 

• Google Chrome (Option 4): An application software (a web browser) used to access the internet.

question: What is the duration of single round in free style wrestling?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 3 min.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Under the rules of United World Wrestling (UWW), a freestyle wrestling bout consists of two periods (rounds) of 3 minutes each, with a short break between periods. (फ्रीस्टाइल कुश्ती — प्रत्येक राउंड 3 मिनट)

 

• The wrestler who scores more technical points, or achieves a fall (pin), technical superiority, or disqualification of the opponent, wins the bout.

 

• Freestyle wrestling allows the use of both upper and lower body holds, unlike Greco-Roman wrestling, which restricts holds to above the waist.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Wrestling is contested at the Olympic Games in both freestyle and Greco-Roman styles, for both men and women (women compete only in freestyle).

 

• India has a strong wrestling tradition, with athletes like Sushil Kumar, Bajrang Punia, and Vinesh Phogat winning international medals.

 

NOTE

 

• 2 min, 3.5 min, 2.5 min (Options 1, 2, 4): None of these match the official UWW round duration of 3 minutes per period in freestyle wrestling.

question: Which of the following teams won the 9th Pro Kabaddi League 2022?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Jaipur Pink Panthers.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Jaipur Pink Panthers won the Season 9 (2022) Pro Kabaddi League (PKL) title, defeating Puneri Paltan in the final. (प्रो कबड्डी लीग सीज़न 9 — जयपुर पिंक पैंथर्स)

 

• This was Jaipur Pink Panthers' second PKL title, having previously won Season 1 as well.

 

• Star raider Deepak Niwas Hooda, who led Jaipur Pink Panthers to the title, was also named the season's Most Valuable Player (MVP).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Puneri Paltan (runners-up in Season 9) went on to win the PKL Season 10 (2023) title.

 

• The Pro Kabaddi League is India's premier professional kabaddi competition, launched in 2014.

 

NOTE

 

• Puneri Paltan (Option 1): Was the runner-up in Season 9, not the champion.

 

• Bengaluru Bulls (Option 3): Won the PKL Season 5 (2017) title, not Season 9.

 

• UP Yoddhas (Option 4): Has not won a PKL title as of Season 9.

question: Name the web portal launched by the Department of Telecommunication sharing information on mobile towers and EMF Emission Compliances.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Tarang Sanchar.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• 'Tarang Sanchar' is a web portal launched by the Department of Telecommunications (DoT), Government of India, to provide the public with information on locations of mobile towers and their Electro-Magnetic Field (EMF) emission compliance status. (तरंग संचार — मोबाइल टावर EMF पोर्टल)

 

• The portal allows citizens to check whether a mobile tower near them complies with prescribed EMF radiation norms and enables telecom operators to self-certify compliance.

 

• It was launched to address public concerns about the safety of EMF radiation from mobile towers.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• BharatNet is a flagship government project to provide broadband internet connectivity to Gram Panchayats across rural India.

 

• The National Optical Fibre Network (NOFN) was the earlier name of the BharatNet project before it was rebranded in 2015.

 

NOTE

 

• Bharat Net (Option 1): A rural broadband connectivity project, not the EMF/mobile-tower information portal.

 

• National Optical Fibre Network (Option 2): The former name of the BharatNet project.

 

• Bharat Sanchar (Option 4): Not the name of any dedicated DoT portal for mobile tower/EMF information (not to be confused with the telecom PSU BSNL).

question: Which south-eastern Dravidian language has been approved by Odisha state to be included in the Eighth Schedule of the Constitution of India, on 10th July 2023?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Kui.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Odisha Cabinet approved a resolution on 10 July 2023 recommending the inclusion of the Kui language — spoken predominantly by the Kondh (Khond) tribal community of Odisha — in the Eighth Schedule of the Constitution of India. (कुई भाषा — ओडिशा, आठवीं अनुसूची)

 

• Kui is classified as a south-eastern Dravidian language.

 

• The Eighth Schedule currently lists 22 scheduled languages; inclusion of a language requires a constitutional amendment by Parliament.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other languages whose inclusion in the Eighth Schedule has been demanded by various states include Bhojpuri, Rajasthani, and Tulu.

 

• The Eighth Schedule languages are used, among other things, for translations of official documents and for candidates to take certain competitive examinations.

 

NOTE

 

• Tulu (Option 1): A Dravidian language spoken mainly in coastal Karnataka (Tulu Nadu) and parts of Kerala, not associated with this Odisha resolution.

 

• Kodagu (Option 2): A Dravidian language spoken in the Kodagu (Coorg) district of Karnataka.

 

• Malto (Option 4): A Dravidian language spoken by the Malo/Mal Paharia tribal communities, mainly in Jharkhand and West Bengal.

question: Who was the first to develop a mathematical predictive heliocentric model of the solar system?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Nicolaus Copernicus.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Nicolaus Copernicus, a Polish astronomer, proposed the first mathematically predictive heliocentric (Sun-centred) model of the solar system in his work 'De revolutionibus orbium coelestium', published in 1543. (सूर्य केंद्रीय सिद्धांत — निकोलस कोपरनिकस)

 

• His model placed the Sun near the centre of the universe, with the Earth and other planets revolving around it, replacing the earlier Earth-centred (geocentric) Ptolemaic model.

 

• This work is regarded as a foundational text of the Copernican Revolution in astronomy.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Galileo Galilei later provided key observational/telescopic evidence (such as the phases of Venus and the moons of Jupiter) supporting the heliocentric model.

 

• Johannes Kepler subsequently refined the model with his laws of planetary motion, showing that planetary orbits are elliptical rather than perfectly circular.

 

NOTE

 

• Pierre-Simon Laplace (Option 1): A later mathematician/astronomer known for his work on celestial mechanics and the nebular hypothesis of solar system formation, not the originator of the heliocentric model.

 

• Immanuel Kant (Option 2): A philosopher who, along with Laplace, contributed to the nebular hypothesis of solar system origin, not the heliocentric model itself.

 

• Galileo Galilei (Option 3): Supported and provided observational evidence for heliocentrism but did not originate the mathematical predictive model — that was Copernicus, decades earlier.

question: Brahmo Samaj was earlier known as:
solution_text:
The correct answer is Bramho Sabha.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Raja Ram Mohan Roy founded the Brahmo Sabha in 1828 in Calcutta as a reformist religious organisation opposing idol worship and social evils like sati. (ब्राह्मो सभा — राजा राम मोहन राय)

 

• The organisation was later renamed Brahmo Samaj in 1830, and it continued under leaders such as Debendranath Tagore after Ram Mohan Roy's death.

 

• The Brahmo Samaj played a key role in the socio-religious reform movements of 19th-century Bengal, campaigning against practices such as sati and child marriage and for widow remarriage.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Brahmo Samaj later split into factions, including the Sadharan Brahmo Samaj, founded by leaders like Keshub Chandra Sen's associates after internal differences.

 

• Ram Mohan Roy is often referred to as the 'Father of Modern India' or 'Father of the Indian Renaissance'.

 

NOTE

 

• Veda Samaj (Option 1): Founded in Madras in 1864, influenced by Brahmo ideas but a separate organisation, not an earlier name of Brahmo Samaj.

 

• Prarthana Samaj (Option 2): Founded in Bombay in 1867 by Atmaram Pandurang, inspired by Brahmo Samaj but a distinct organisation.

 

• Arya Samaj (Option 3): Founded by Swami Dayanand Saraswati in 1875, an entirely separate reform organisation.

question: Which of the following committees recommended the inclusion of fundamental duties in the Constitution of India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Swaran Singh Committee.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Swaran Singh Committee, constituted in 1976, recommended adding a separate chapter on Fundamental Duties to the Constitution of India. (स्वर्ण सिंह समिति — मौलिक कर्तव्य)

 

• Based on its recommendations, the 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1976 inserted Article 51A in Part IVA of the Constitution, originally listing 10 fundamental duties (an 11th was added later by the 86th Amendment, 2002).

 

• The concept of fundamental duties was inspired by the Constitution of the erstwhile USSR.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Fundamental duties are enumerated in the Constitution but are not legally enforceable in court like fundamental rights.

 

• The 11th fundamental duty, added in 2002, relates to a parent's/guardian's duty to provide educational opportunities to their child aged 6-14 years.

 

NOTE

 

• Balwant Rai Mehta Committee (Option 1): Recommended the three-tier Panchayati Raj system in 1957.

 

• Sarkaria Committee (Option 2): Examined Centre-State relations and submitted its report in 1988.

 

• Raja Mannar Committee (Option 4): A Tamil Nadu state committee that examined Centre-State relations, unrelated to fundamental duties.

question:
What happens in case of market equilibrium:

(a) Market demand = market supply

(b) There is no excess supply in the market
solution_text:
The correct answer is Both (a) and (b).

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Market equilibrium occurs at the price where quantity demanded equals quantity supplied, i.e., market demand = market supply, so statement (a) is correct. (बाजार संतुलन — मांग = आपूर्ति)

 

• At this equilibrium price, there is neither excess supply (surplus) nor excess demand (shortage) in the market, so statement (b) is also correct.

 

• If price is set above equilibrium, supply exceeds demand (excess supply); if set below equilibrium, demand exceeds supply (excess demand, or shortage).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The equilibrium price is also called the market-clearing price, since at this price all goods offered for sale are bought.

 

• Shifts in demand or supply curves (due to changes in income, price of related goods, technology, etc.) lead to a new equilibrium price and quantity.

 

NOTE

 

• Neither (a) nor (b) (Option 1): Incorrect, as both statements correctly describe market equilibrium.

 

• Only (a) (Option 2): Incorrect, as statement (b) is also true at equilibrium.

 

• Only (b) (Option 4): Incorrect, as statement (a) is also true at equilibrium.

question: Bhavai is a dance form that belongs to which of the following states?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Rajasthan.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Bhavai is a popular folk dance form of Rajasthan, known for performers (often women) balancing multiple earthen pots or brass pitchers on their heads while dancing, sometimes on the edge of a sword, on glass, or atop a brass thali. (भवाई नृत्य — राजस्थान)

 

• It is traditionally performed by communities such as the Bhil and Kalbelia communities of Rajasthan during festivals and special occasions.

 

• The dance demonstrates remarkable balance and grace, often performed to the accompaniment of folk instruments like the *dholak* and *harmonium*.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Note that 'Bhavai' is also the name of a distinct folk theatre tradition of Gujarat, which combines dance, music and acting — different from the Rajasthani Bhavai dance.

 

• Other well-known folk dances of Rajasthan include Ghoomar, Kalbelia, and Chari.

 

NOTE

 

• Odisha, Madhya Pradesh, Bihar (Options 2, 3, 4): None of these states is associated with the Bhavai dance form, which is specifically identified with Rajasthan.

question: Mahavir Jayanti celebrates the birthday of Lord Mahavira who is the _______ Tirthankara of Jainism.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 24th.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Lord Mahavira (Vardhamana) was the 24th and last Tirthankara of Jainism, and Mahavir Jayanti celebrates his birth anniversary. (महावीर जयंती — 24वें तीर्थंकर)

 

• He is traditionally believed to have been born around 599 BCE at Kundagrama, near Vaishali (in present-day Bihar).

 

• He attained Kevala Jnana (omniscience) after years of penance and attained nirvana (moksha) at Pawapuri.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The 23rd Tirthankara, Parshvanatha, preceded Mahavira and is believed to have lived about 250 years earlier.

 

• Jainism recognises a total of 24 Tirthankaras, the first being Rishabhanatha (Adinatha).

 

NOTE

 

• 25th, 26th (Options 1, 2): There is no 25th or 26th Tirthankara; the tradition recognises only 24.

 

• 23rd (Option 3): This was Parshvanatha, not Mahavira.

question: Which of the following causes enlargement and extension growth of cells?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Turgor pressure.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Turgor pressure is the pressure exerted by the water-filled contents of a plant cell against its cell wall; this pressure drives the enlargement and extension growth of cells. (स्फीति दाब — कोशिका वृद्धि)

 

• As water enters the cell by osmosis, the resulting turgor pressure pushes against the relatively elastic cell wall, causing the cell to expand and elongate.

 

• Turgor pressure is also essential for maintaining the rigidity of non-woody plant parts and for processes like the opening and closing of stomata.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Loss of turgor pressure (due to water loss) causes wilting in plants.

 

• Osmosis is the underlying process by which water moves into plant cells, ultimately generating turgor pressure.

 

NOTE

 

• Imbibition (Option 1): The absorption of water by solids such as seeds or dry wood, causing them to swell; it is not the process specifically responsible for cell extension growth.

 

• Pressure potential (Option 2): A component of water potential related to turgor, but the growth-driving force itself is specifically termed turgor pressure.

 

• Osmotic pressure (Option 3): Relates to the movement of water into the cell via osmosis, which precedes and contributes to turgor pressure, but is not itself the cause of cell extension.

question: In July 2021, which of the following persons declared herself/himself brand ambassador of 'Khadi Prakritik Paint', made from cow dung by the Khadi and Village Industries Commission?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Nitin Gadkari.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Union Minister Nitin Gadkari launched 'Khadi Prakritik Paint', an eco-friendly paint made from cow dung by the Khadi and Village Industries Commission (KVIC), and declared himself its brand ambassador. (खादी प्राकृतिक पेंट — नितिन गडकरी)

 

• The paint was launched in January 2021 and is notable for being odourless, low-cost, and free from heavy metals such as lead, mercury, and chromium/arsenic.

 

• The initiative also aims to provide additional income to cattle owners/farmers by using cow dung as a raw material.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• KVIC also developed 'Khadi Prakritik Paint' in two variants: distemper paint and emulsion paint.

 

• KVIC functions under the Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSME).

 

NOTE

 

• Nirmala Sitharaman, Narendra Singh Tomar, Rajnath Singh (Options 2, 3, 4): None of these ministers was associated with the launch or brand ambassadorship of Khadi Prakritik Paint.

question: In which year was the Marris College of Music established in India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1926.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Marris College of Music was established in 1926 in Lucknow by the eminent musicologist Pandit Vishnu Narayan Bhatkhande. (मैरिस कॉलेज ऑफ म्यूज़िक — 1926)

 

• It was named after Sir William Marris, who was then the Governor of the United Provinces and supported the institution's establishment.

 

• The college was later renamed Bhatkhande Sangeet Vidyapith (now Bhatkhande Music Institute Deemed University) in honour of its founder.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• V. N. Bhatkhande is also renowned for classifying Hindustani classical ragas into ten thaats (parent scales).

 

• Lucknow, as the seat of this institution, became an important centre for the systematic study and teaching of Hindustani classical music.

 

NOTE

 

• 1919, 1901, 1922 (Options 1, 2, 4): None of these corresponds to the actual founding year of the Marris College of Music, which was 1926.

question: In MS Word, which option allows you to insert a new column in a table while simultaneously shifting the existing columns to the right?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Insert Column to the Left.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• In Microsoft Word's table tools, "Insert Column to the Left" inserts a new blank column immediately before the column where the cursor currently is, which pushes that column — and every column after it — one position to the right. (टेबल में कॉलम जोड़ना — बाईं ओर सम्मिलित करें)

 

• This option is found under Table Tools → Layout tab → Rows & Columns group, alongside "Insert Column to the Right," "Insert Row Above," and "Insert Row Below."

 

• By contrast, "Insert Column to the Right" inserts the new column immediately after the cursor's column, so the cursor's own column does not move — only columns further to the right shift.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The same logic applies to rows: "Insert Row Above" shifts the current row (and everything below it) downward, while "Insert Row Below" does not move the current row.

 

• Right-clicking inside a table cell and choosing Insert → Insert Columns to the Left/Right provides the same functionality via the context menu.

 

NOTE

 

• Insert Column to the Right (Option 1): Adds a column after the cursor's column without shifting that column itself — does not match the "shift existing columns to the right" description in the question.

 

• Insert Columns (Option 2): Not a standard, distinctly labelled Word ribbon command matching this specific column-shifting behaviour.

 

• Insert Table (Option 3): Creates an entirely new table; it does not add a column to an existing table.

question: Which of the following is NOT a part of Carnatic music?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Dhrupad.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Dhrupad is one of the oldest and most serious vocal genres of Hindustani (North Indian) classical music — it is not a part of Carnatic (South Indian) music. (कर्नाटक संगीत — ध्रुपद हिंदुस्तानी शैली)

 

• Varnam, Pallavi, and Charana are all genuine compositional elements/forms found in Carnatic music.

 

• A Varnam is typically the opening item of a Carnatic concert, designed to showcase the raga's grammar and the performer's technical command.

 

• Pallavi refers to the opening theme/refrain line of a Carnatic composition (such as a kriti), which is elaborated melodically and rhythmically; Charana refers to a concluding stanza/section found in Carnatic compositions like varnams and kritis.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Famous exponents of Dhrupad include the Dagar family, associated with the Dagarvani gharana.

 

• Common forms in Carnatic music also include the Kriti, Ragam-Tanam-Pallavi, Javali, and Thillana.

 

NOTE

 

• Varnam (Option 1): A genuine, foundational compositional form in Carnatic music.

 

• Pallavi (Option 3): A genuine structural component (the opening theme) of Carnatic compositions.

 

• Charana (Option 4): A genuine structural component (a concluding stanza) of Carnatic compositions.

question: According to the Department of Industrial Policy and Promotion (now the Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade, DPIIT), which one of the following is NOT a core industry?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Jute.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Index of Eight Core Industries, compiled by the Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade (DPIIT), Ministry of Commerce and Industry, tracks the combined and individual performance of eight key infrastructure sectors of the Indian economy. (आठ प्रमुख उद्योग — उद्योग संवर्धन विभाग)

 

• The eight core industries are: Coal, Crude Oil, Natural Gas, Refinery Products, Fertilizers, Steel, Cement, and Electricity. Jute is not one of them.

 

• Together, these eight industries account for about 40.27% of the weight of items included in the Index of Industrial Production (IIP).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Among the eight core industries, Refinery Products carries the highest weight in the index, while Fertilizers carries the lowest.

 

• Jute cultivation, production, and trade in India are instead monitored by bodies such as the Jute Corporation of India and the National Jute Board.

 

NOTE

 

• Electricity (Option 1): One of the eight core industries tracked by DPIIT.

 

• Fertilizers (Option 3): One of the eight core industries tracked by DPIIT.

 

• Crude Oil (Option 4): One of the eight core industries tracked by DPIIT.
